dialogue_quality_notes: Participants moved from complaint to concrete proposals and bargaining quickly (natural negotiation).
Some repeated lines (Agent C's 'I'm not the house cleaner' repeated twice; Agent B repeated extractor request), but repetition did not stall resolution.
All proposals and counterproposals stayed consistent with the known facts (one stove, shared pans, ventilation).
Agreements included conditional trade-offs (exclusive nights in exchange for supplies/cleaning), which is constructive.
evaluation.final_reason: The household reached a concrete agreement in Round 5: everyone accepted the wash-and-vent rule and a scheduling method where each person picks two weeknights; Agent A agreed to allow Agent D two late weeknights conditional on heads-ups and contribution to supplies/cleaning, and Agent D accepted and chose specific nights. Key lines: Agent A: "whoever uses shared pans washes them the same day, and we open the window/turn on the extractor when cooking." Agent A (conditional acceptance): "You can have two late weeknights—pick them now, give a heads-up before you cook, and help with supplies or do cleaning." Agent D (acceptance and specifics): "I'll take Tuesday and Thursday as my two late weeknights. I'll give a heads-up before I cook, and I'll help buy supplies." These statements show mutual spoken agreement on who does what (washing same day, use extractor, schedule, D buys supplies and gives notice), so the remaining substantive issues were settled in Round 5.
position_change_notes: Agent A moved from proposing simple rules and rejecting a strict rota to endorsing a flexible two-night-per-person approach with conditional concessions: Turn 1 vs Turn 9/11.
Agent C consistently insisted on everyone washing their own pans and agreed to wash the pan immediately; retained position on fairness while complying with immediate request: Turn 3 and Turn 7.
Agent D proposed a strict schedule but accepted the preference-based two-night solution and secured two late nights by offering to buy supplies and give notice: Turn 4 then Turn 10.
Agent B consistently supported the rules and scheduling idea and pressed for immediate compliance with extractor use and pan washing (no substantive change of position).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A proposes household rules and directly asks Agent C to wash last night's pan now: "...whoever uses shared pans washes them the same day, and we open the window/turn on the extractor when cooking. Agent C, please wash last night's pan now." Agent B supports the rules and repeats the demand, but Agent C has not yet responded.

Agent C accepts washing the pan but objects to being singled out and insists on everyone washing their own pans: "I'll wash the pan now. But I'm not the house cleaner: if we're doing rules, everyone should wash their own pans the same day and not just point at one person." Agent D introduces a new scheduling proposal (stove rota). The normative issue of who is responsible for washing and how to manage stove time becomes explicit.

Agent A rejects a strict rota and offers a softer alternative: "Let's each pick two preferred weeknights. If you need a night, ask ahead. If you want exclusive nights, help with supplies or do extra cleaning." Agent B accepts the two-night idea. The dispute shifts from a strict rota to a preference-based arrangement but remains unsettled.

Agent C reiterates the wash-everyone rule: "...everyone washes their own pans the same day." Agent D accepts the wash-and-vent rule and restates the two-weeknight cooking idea while requesting two late nights for himself. Positions are converging but D's request for late nights is a new specific demand that remains unresolved.

Agent A accepts D's late-night request with conditions: "You can have two late weeknights—pick them now, give a heads-up before you cook, and help with supplies or do cleaning." Agent D picks specific nights and agrees to heads-up and buying supplies: "I'll take Tuesday and Thursday as my two late weeknights. I'll give a heads-up before I cook, and I'll help buy supplies." This round records concrete mutual commitments on washing/venting, scheduling, and supplies, settling the main substantive issues.

Agent A reiterates the agreed conditions: "Tuesday and Thursday works. Give a heads-up before you cook, and please chip in for supplies." Agent B repeats the immediate request to use extractor and window and asks if the pan is washed: "...tonight I need the extractor on and the window open. Agent C, is the pan washed?" No new substantive disagreement is introduced and the agreements from round 5 remain in place.

substantive_insights: The main tension combined two issues: immediate annoyance (smell/unwashed pan) and ongoing scheduling/effort fairness; resolving both required rules and a sharing mechanism.
A compromise approach (preferred nights plus heads-ups) resolved the rota dispute without imposing a strict schedule.
Conditioning exclusive or preferred nights on extra contributions (supplies/cleaning) was an effective bargaining move that satisfied both convenience and fairness concerns.
Concrete, specific commitments (named nights, promise to buy supplies, promise to wash same day) enabled settlement in a speech-only transcript.

normalizations: Adjusted resolution_round from 5 to 6 to match the conflict trajectory.
